key_insight: Multilingual multimodal machine learning can accurately distinguish nonfluent/agrammatic from logopenic PPA in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals using connected speech from either language.
clinical_relevance: This suggests a scalable support tool for bilingual aphasia assessment that could reduce reliance on lengthy specialist testing and help address language-access barriers.
method: 34 Catalan-Spanish simultaneous bilingual patients were recorded describing a picture in both dominant and non-dominant languages.
Four feature sets were extracted: speech timing, word-level parameters, linguistic features, and image-text congruence.
These features were tested in machine-learning classifiers and combined in an ensemble model.
evidence_signal: In 34 patients (24 lvPPA, 10 nfvPPA), the best models reached macro F1 scores of 93% in the non-dominant language and 92% in the dominant language, with no significant performance difference between languages.
watch_item: Small sample size and single-task speech elicitation mean the approach needs broader validation before routine clinical use.
paper_title: Differentiating nonfluent/agrammatic and logopenic primary progressive aphasia in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals by applying multilingual multimodal machine learning to connected speech
